summary: Orchestrator rewrites idempotency baggage header causing split tool executions across language SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightForms reports duplicated external tool/webhook invocations when their orchestration layer proxies requests between a TypeScript frontend, a Python worker, and a Go webhook. The duplicates only occur after a retry path is taken (client or SDK retry).

Impact:
- External webhook receives 2 distinct executions for what customer expects to be a single logical tool call.
- Observable with ~1.6% of requests that hit the retry window in us-east; affects live traffic for BrightForms (enterprise, high volume ingestion).

Environment:
- Customer tier: enterprise
- Region: prod/us-east (us-east-1)
- SDKs in use: TS SDK v1.9.0, Python SDK v0.14.2, Go SDK v0.8.3
- Orchestrator: customer-managed proxy (k8s sidecar) that rewrites request headers for internal routing

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) TS client sends a streaming request with function_call enabled and includes X-RW-Idempotency header set from frontend (base64-url-no-pad token).
2) Request routes through customer's orchestrator sidecar which inspects and rewrites headers for tenancy tracing (adds X-Tenant, X-Trace).
3) Python worker receives the stream, executes a funcall that triggers an outbound POST to their webhook. The SDK attaches the idempotency token to the webhook POST for deduplication downstream.
4) Under network jitter the TS SDK triggers an automatic retry; the orchestrator proxies the retry path but performs a header decode/encode step when copying the idempotency baggage into an internal header (X-RW-Idemp-Baggage).
5) Downstream the webhook receives two different idempotency tokens and processes the function twice.

Observed behavior:
- Two distinct idempotency token values in server logs for the retries (tokens differ by padding and by url-safe vs standard base64 variants).
- Python SDK retains original header name for outgoing webhooks, but the orchestrator-inserted baggage header is used by a different service for dedupe, leading to mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- Idempotency token should be canonicalized and preserved across proxies so retries do not create new logical requests. SDKs should document canonical encoding and negotiable header name.

Temporary workaround provided by Support:
- Instructed customer to configure their sidecar to copy X-RW-Idempotency verbatim to internal services (avoid decode/re-encode) and to normalize to a single header name.
- Suggested short-term: have webhook dedupe look at both header variants (X-RW-Idempotency and X-RW-Idemp-Baggage) until canonicalization is fixed.

Attachments:
- Customer trace dump (redacted) showing headers at each hop (attached in ticket).
- Excerpt of Python worker logs included below in investigation notes.

investigation_notes: Reproduction: built a local proxy that takes X-RW-Idempotency (url-safe b64, no pad), base64-decodes then re-encodes with standard base64 (adds +/=). When the retry occurs the dedupe key changes and webhook processes twice.
Observed pattern: token variants differ only in charset and padding; length and underlying bytes are identical when decoded. Dedupe service compares raw header string, not decoded bytes.

Hypothesis: two options to fix - (A) require proxies to pass header through unchanged, or (B) move dedupe to decode-and-compare-by-bytes canonicalization on server side. (B) is safer but requires runtime change in webhook dedupe logic.

Experiment: modified local dedupe to base64-decode both header variants and compare bytes. This eliminated duplicates in the test harness. However this change must be applied consistently in all webhook handlers (customer and Redwood-managed).

Cross-language: TS, Python, Go SDKs differ in their default Base64 functions. TS client uses Buffer.toString('base64url') no-pad; Go client used encoding/base64.URLEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding) in recent versions but some internal proxies still use StdEncoding.
Risk: any change that silently normalizes on Redwood side could break integrations expecting raw string equality in logs. Recommend opt-in behavior with compatibility guidance.
Related: SUP-271828 shows earlier idempotency key normalization discussions; link added for context.
resolution: Workaround applied by customer (preserve X-RW-Idempotency verbatim) reduced duplicates to zero. Engineering change merged: agent-middleware PR #412 adds a header-preserve flag and a canonicalization utility that can be enabled at proxy level. SDK note added to docs advising base64-url-no-pad canonical form. Action items: roll out middleware flag in a canary to 10% of customers next week, and follow-up to add server-side dedupe decode-and-compare in webhook handlers as longer-term fix.
resolution_notes: Patch: github.com/redwood-inference/agent-middleware/pull/412 merged (adds preserve_header config and docs).
SDK docs: Updated Idempotency section to document canonical encoding (base64-url no padding) and recommended header name X-RW-Idempotency in SDK changelogs.
Rollout plan: canary deploy middleware flag to 10% of gateway traffic in us-east on 2026-03-18; monitor dup rate metric (metric: webhook.dup_rate).
Customer follow-up: BrightForms confirmed temporary workaround and requested notification when canary completes. Assigned follow-up owner: Aisha Patel.
Longer term: implement server-side dedupe decode-and-compare in shared webhook library (ticket INT-135791 created to track internal work).
